candidate.title: TAIL-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina schematic overview of TAIL-seq: a single route from rRNA-depleted RNA through biotinylated 3′ adapter ligation, RNase T1 partial digestion, streptavidin capture, 5′ phosphorylation, gel purification, 5′ adapter ligation and a broad RT/PCR/purification block to cDNA. The far-left yellow-highlighted RNA and measurement caption are a descriptive target icon, not an additional processing branch. Text-supported readout interpretation is included without adding a sequencing operation to the drawing. This scope does not include PAL-seq, PAT-Seq, RNA Tagging or ribosome profiling, which occur only in comparison or reference material.

states.label: rRNA-depleted RNA
features: Diagram starts after rRNA depletion; a representative mRNA is shown as a purple body with a variable-length 3′ poly(A) tail, AAAA(A)n.
This is an rRNA-depleted RNA population, not a claim of pure mRNA or of oligo(dT)-selected input.

evidence.locator: Main route left: rRNA-depleted RNA, purple strand ending AAAA(A)n
Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is first removed from total RNA by affinity-based depletion.

states.label: RNA bearing a biotinylated 3′ adapter
features: Orange adapter is joined beyond the original RNA 3′ extremity; purple RNA body and poly(A) tail remain connected.
The terminal blue star is interpreted as the biotin affinity handle from the catalogue description and its subsequent streptavidin binding; the image provides no star legend.

evidence.locator: 3′ adaptor ligation: purple RNA–AAAA–orange adapter–blue star
Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: After purification, mRNAs are ligated to biotinylated 3' adapters prior to RNase T1 fragmentation and purified further by streptavidin pull-down.

evidence.locator: Blue star on the orange 3′ adapter before capture and in contact with the streptavidin support
evidence.rationale: The star is not explicitly labeled. Its location on the adapter and its subsequent contact with the support, together with the catalogue statement that the adapter is biotinylated, support interpreting it as the biotin affinity handle; no detailed tag structure is inferred.

states.label: Partially digested adapter-tagged RNA population
features: Short detached purple pieces and a remaining RNA-body segment contiguous with the poly(A) tail and the tagged 3′ adapter are drawn.
The retained terminal fragment physically associates proximal transcript sequence, tail and original terminal sequence with the 3′ adapter.

evidence.locator: Partial digestion with RNase T1: separated purple pieces and tail-bearing adapter-tagged terminal fragment
Full text [b00017], TAIL-Seq paragraph
evidence.quote: TAIL-Seq involves the ligation of a biotin-containing adapter to the 3′ end of mRNAs, followed by a partial digestion by RNase T1, which cleaves downstream of guanosine, thus protecting the poly(A) tail.
evidence.rationale: Secondary review full text supports cleavage specificity; this is not direct inspection of the original protocol.

states.label: Streptavidin-bound adapter-bearing terminal RNA fragments
features: The blue-star tag contacts the streptavidin support; this is an attachment change, not RNA-to-cDNA conversion.
RNA body segment, poly(A) tail and 3′ adapter remain connected in the retained route.

evidence.locator: Pull down with streptavidin: tagged terminal RNA bound through blue star to blue/gray support
Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: After purification, mRNAs are ligated to biotinylated 3' adapters prior to RNase T1 fragmentation and purified further by streptavidin pull-down.

states.label: Selected terminal RNA fragments with phosphorylated 5′ ends
features: Input history includes 3′ adapter ligation, RNase T1 partial digestion and streptavidin capture.
5′ phosphorylation is explicitly captioned; no phosphate chemical symbol is drawn.
Attachment to the support during this captioned step is not resolved by the drawing.

evidence.locator: 5′ end phosphorylation caption and rightward arrow following captured RNA
Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: The 5' ends are phosphorylated and size-selected for 500–1000 nt fragments to prevent short noncoding RNA (ncRNA) fragments from contaminating the sequence data.

states.label: Gel-purified terminal RNA fragments with phosphorylated 5′ ends
features: Selected fragments retain proximal RNA sequence, poly(A) tail, biotinylated 3′ adapter and 5′ phosphorylation history.
Size selection reduces short ncRNA contamination; this does not prove complete mRNA specificity.
The support is absent from this panel; the blue-star tag remains on the 3′ adapter. Release from the support is not separately depicted.

evidence.locator: Gel purify caption and shortened tail-bearing RNA with orange adapter and blue star; support absent
Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: The 5' ends are phosphorylated and size-selected for 500–1000 nt fragments to prevent short noncoding RNA (ncRNA) fragments from contaminating the sequence data.

states.label: Terminal RNA fragments carrying adapters at both ends
features: A new green 5′ adapter joins the purple RNA body segment; the tail and orange biotinylated 3′ adapter remain at the other end.
The insert represents the RNA 3′ extremity and adjacent transcript sequence, rather than the full transcript.

evidence.locator: 5′ adaptor ligation: new green segment at left of purple RNA; 3′ tag retained
Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: The phosphorylated 5' ends are ligated to 5' adapters, reverse-transcribed, PCR-amplified, and sequenced.

states.label: Purified amplified cDNA library
features: Rightmost product is labeled cDNA and uses green/blue/orange segments to represent adapter-flanked DNA derived from the selected terminal RNA inserts.
cDNA is the sequencing carrier; it encodes the RNA tail and terminal sequence together with proximal transcript sequence.
Paired-end sequencing links transcript identification from one end to tail-length information from the other; the original method also measures 3′ terminal modifications.
Homopolymer readout uses fluorescence re-analysis to reduce poly(A)-length overestimation; PCR is reported to be unfavorable for homopolymeric sequences.

operations.label: 3′ adaptor ligation
operations.description: Join an adapter carrying a biotin affinity handle to the RNA 3′ end, producing tagged RNA before fragmentation.
operations.mechanism: 3′ adapter ligation; the catalogue identifies the adapter as biotinylated.
operations.information_effect: Tags the original 3′ extremity for later retention without requiring an oligo(dT) enrichment step.

evidence.locator: 3′ adaptor ligation: purple RNA–AAAA–orange adapter–blue star
Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: After purification, mRNAs are ligated to biotinylated 3' adapters prior to RNase T1 fragmentation and purified further by streptavidin pull-down.

evidence.locator: Description / advantages / limitations
evidence.quote: Eliminates bias toward long poly(A) because it does not use oligo(dT) enrichment

operations.label: Partial digestion with RNase T1
operations.description: Partially cleave RNA bodies, producing detached upstream fragments and an adapter-bearing terminal fragment with the tail still attached.
operations.mechanism: RNase T1 partial digestion; the inspected full-text review reports cleavage downstream of guanosine, which spares the poly(A) tract.
operations.information_effect: Reduces the represented RNA to terminal fragments while preserving tail-to-proximal-sequence linkage. The diagram does not represent intact full-length mRNA after this step.

Full text [b00017], TAIL-Seq paragraph
evidence.quote: TAIL-Seq involves the ligation of a biotin-containing adapter to the 3′ end of mRNAs, followed by a partial digestion by RNase T1, which cleaves downstream of guanosine, thus protecting the poly(A) tail.
evidence.rationale: Secondary review full text supports cleavage specificity; this is not direct inspection of the original protocol.

operations.label: Pull down with streptavidin
operations.description: Capture the biotin-tagged terminal RNA on streptavidin support; the retained route changes from free fragmented RNA to support-bound RNA.
operations.information_effect: Enriches fragments that carry the ligated 3′ adapter over detached upstream pieces; tag retention itself is not proof that every captured molecule is mRNA.

operations.label: 5′ end phosphorylation
operations.description: Phosphorylate the 5′ ends of captured terminal RNA fragments, producing the phosphorylated substrate used downstream.
operations.mechanism: 5′ end phosphorylation is stated; no enzyme or detailed end-repair chemistry is specified in the drawing.
operations.information_effect: Prepares the retained fragment 5′ ends for the depicted 5′ adapter ligation while retaining the 3′ end association.

operations.label: Gel purify
operations.description: Gel-purify the phosphorylated terminal RNA fragments to obtain the size-selected population shown without its capture support.
operations.mechanism: Gel-based size selection; catalogue explains selection against short ncRNA fragments. Support-release chemistry is not shown.
operations.information_effect: Further restricts the fragment population and reduces short ncRNA contamination; retains the linked transcript/tail/3′ adapter insert.

operations.label: 5′ adaptor ligation
operations.description: Join the green 5′ adapter to the phosphorylated terminal RNA fragment, producing an RNA insert flanked by 5′ and 3′ adapters.
operations.mechanism: 5′ adapter ligation to the phosphorylated RNA end.
operations.information_effect: Adds the second library interface while preserving the proximal-sequence-to-tail association.

The method association is established by the original paper abstract, with detailed preparation supported by the diagram, catalogue and inspected full-text review.

unknowns.question: At what point, and by what interface, is the captured RNA released from the streptavidin support relative to 5′ phosphorylation and gel purification? The bead is drawn at capture and absent in the gel-purified panel, but neither the diagram nor inspected supplied text specifies a release operation or attachment state during phosphorylation. A relevant primary-method passage would resolve this local attachment boundary; no release chemistry is inferred.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the complete schematic-level architecture. All seven captioned transformations and their retained material route are represented, including RNase-generated detached fragments within s2, affinity attachment in s3, the stated 5′ end change, both adapter interfaces, and conversion from RNA to amplified cDNA. No retained branch or depicted alternative is omitted; the far-left measurement icon has no connecting processing arrow. The single-method scope and all eight distinct reference assessments are supported. The primary paper is available here as metadata and abstract only; detailed preparation is supported by the diagram, catalogue, and explicitly identified secondary full-text review. No consequential source conflict requiring a correction was found. The unshown support-release procedure is appropriately left unspecified in u1 and does not obstruct this declared schematic scope.
